title: Nager.Date public holidays API (Italy, national holidays by year)
summary: Nager.Date REST endpoint returning the national public holidays for a given year and ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code. For this use case the call is PublicHolidays/{year}/IT, which returns one JSON record per national holiday date (about 13 to 14 records per year). It covers national holidays only, not regional or patron-saint days, and does not include bridge days. Probes for 2023, 2024 and 2026 returned HTTP 200 with dates in each requested year; 2025 was not probed.

spatial.notes: National scope only (global=true in probed records). Regional and local holidays in northern Italy are not returned by this call. Start and end dates reflect the years probed (2023, 2024, 2026), not a documented coverage period.

licence.evidence: Register api.nager_public_holidays: agreement_status 'not_required_open_data', approved_purposes ['prototyping','production'], terms_url https://github.com/nager/Nager.Date. probe_url of that page shows 'MIT license' for the repository and links to /nager/Nager.Date/blob/main/LICENSE. That licence text was not read and it is not established that it covers the holiday data itself.

access.request_process: GET https://date.nager.at/api/v3/PublicHolidays/{year}/{country}; no key required in the probes. Register lists the endpoint and path_params year and country.

documentation_excerpts: Register param_notes: 'country is ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 (PT, GB, FR, ...).'
Repository README (probe_url): 'Easily access public holidays for 200+ countries via .NET, REST API, Docker, or NuGet'; 'MIT license'.
quality_notes: Coverage gap for N4 and N5: national holidays only. Regional and patron-saint days in northern Italy are not returned and need a separate source.
Weekend holidays are returned with their date; the source has no weekday field, so the weekday effect must be computed by the analyst.

Probes: 2023 returned 13 records (2023-01-01 to 2023-12-26); 2024 returned 13 records (2024-01-01 to 2024-12-26); 2026 returned 14 records (2026-01-01 to 2026-12-26). Easter Sunday dates (2023-04-09, 2024-03-31, 2026-04-05) are included. All probes returned HTTP 200 JSON. Completeness was not checked against an external holiday list.
2025 was not probed, so the history window (2023-06-01 to 2025-05-31) is only partly verified. The recent window (to 2026-03-31) is covered by the 2026 probe.
Register gives no update cadence or data-vintage date; no data changelog was read.
The register's terms_url points to the GitHub repository. The MIT licence shown there is for the code; no statement about the licence of the holiday data was found in the sources read.
